title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: THE SINGING PLOW
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Hector Alvarado, a forty-nine-year-old snowplow driver in Bangor, Maine.
Hector says about ten words a week.
But alone in his plow at three in the morning, he sings. Loud.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE OPEN RADIO
segments.quote: Practicing an art, no matter how well or badly, is a way to make your soul grow, for heaven's sake.
segments.author: Kurt Vonnegut
lines: One night his elbow pressed the radio button. Every truck in Bangor heard him sing.
Next morning, dispatcher Marcy slid a flyer across the desk. The Bangor Community Chorus needed men.
Hector said he couldn't. Marcy pointed to a Kurt Vonnegut line taped to her screen:
Practicing an art, no matter how well or badly, is a way to make your soul grow, for heaven's sake.
So on Thursday, Hector went.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE AUDITION
segments.quote: When we are listened to, it creates us, makes us unfold and expand.
segments.author: Brenda Ueland
lines: At the audition his voice cracked like an old pickup on a cold morning.
The director, Evelyn, a retired lounge singer, didn't wince. She asked why he sang.
And Hector talked for ten whole minutes. His mom's kitchen radio. Those long, dark roads.
Evelyn smiled. The writer Brenda Ueland said it best:
When we are listened to, it creates us, makes us unfold and expand.
Then he sang again. No crack.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: TOO LOUD
segments.quote: A good listener is not only popular everywhere, but after a while he gets to know something.
segments.author: Wilson Mizner
lines: At rehearsal Hector sang like he was still alone in the truck. Nobody else could be heard.
Walt, an eighty-year-old tenor, leaned over and quoted Wilson Mizner, the old Broadway wit:
A good listener is not only popular everywhere, but after a while he gets to know something.
So Hector sang softer and listened. The whole room started to blend.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE STORM
segments.quote: Do the duty which lies nearest thee.
segments.author: Thomas Carlyle
lines: Concert night, a nor'easter rolled in.
The depot called. Every plow was needed.
Hector thought of his grandpa's favorite Thomas Carlyle line:
Do the duty which lies nearest thee.
So he plowed. But he plowed Hammond Street first, right to the hall.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: LIGHTS OUT
segments.quote: All things are possible until they are proved impossible.
segments.author: Pearl S. Buck
lines: At seven, the power went out. Two hundred people sat in the dark. Evelyn said to cancel.
Marcy on the radio quoted Pearl S. Buck, the author:
All things are possible until they are proved impossible.
Hector parked his plow at the big window. Headlights flooded the stage.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE SOLO
segments.quote: Music expresses that which cannot be said and on which it is impossible to be silent.
segments.author: Victor Hugo
lines: Hector sang the last carol alone, still in his orange vest.
His gruff boss Sully wiped his eyes and blamed the snow.
Evelyn whispered a Victor Hugo line, from the French writer:
Music expresses that which cannot be said and on which it is impossible to be silent.
Now every storm, the night crew asks Hector for one song on the radio.

segments.head: SIX WISE WORDS
segments.quote: Try. Be heard. Listen. Do your duty. Don't quit. Sing.
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: So try badly, let yourself be heard, listen more, do your duty, don't quit in the dark, and sing.
Me? I sing in the shower. My wife calls it the weather alert.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
